items.canonicalSource: 19.01-ticket-config-scaling-allocations/19.01.02-capacity-manifest-allocations-holds.md:214 (D-06) — "The manifest's invariant is `capacity = killed + held + comp + paid + carted + remaining`, enforced at every mutation, never reconciled on a schedule"; corroborated by 19.01.02:34 (the rendered identity), 19.01.02:43 ("| `carted` | Reserved to a buyer mid-checkout (`19.02.04`) | Cart hold create/expire |") and 19.01.02:44 ("| `remaining` | Sellable right now | Derived — never written directly |")
items.summary: 19.05.01's counter table had no `carted` row and defined `remaining` as `capacity − killed − held − paid − comp`, which is 19.01.02 D-06's `remaining` PLUS `carted`. Resolved toward D-06: `carted` is now a first-class counter in 19.05.01 and `remaining` is net of it. Two stale prose lines inside 19.01.02 itself (:122, :154) that read as if `carted` sat inside `remaining` were realigned to D-06. One genuine residual sub-question surfaced by the fix is tracked as 19.05.01 Q-04.
items.classificationRationale: One side is a numbered, named decision in the file that owns the concept — 19.01.02 D-06 owns the manifest identity, and 19.01.02:46 explicitly cedes only the *reporting* of the counters to 19.05.01 ("The counters themselves are owned and reported by `19.05.01`; the manifest is the state, the live count is its reporting face"). The other side is a parenthetical formula in a table cell, with no numbered decision behind it, in a sub-domain where the string `carted` did not appear at all — the signature of an omission, not a competing ratification. Three independent canonical corroborations settle the direction beyond doubt: (1) 19.02-on-sale-announce-presale-cx.md:56 (#CX-03) — "if the hold expiry is long relative to the window, a window can appear sold out while nothing has been sold" — which can only be true if carted removes availability; (2) 19.02.04's Edge Case row "Cart hold too long relative to a small allocation | Window appears sold out while nothing has been sold"; (3) 19.02.04 Q-04, resolved on exactly that quote. The opposite reading (carted inside remaining) would have the storefront boolean report available inventory that no Fan can buy, which contradicts 19.05.01 D-04's own stated posture that a remaining-derived availability signal "is usually untrue once holds are counted" is the thing being fixed, not the thing being shipped. No owner judgement is required: the tree already decided, in the owning file, and one reporting surface drifted.
items.fixApplied: 19.05.01 — (a) Overview:10 counter enumeration now lists `carted`. (b) Counter table:36 gained a **Carted** row defining it as reserved-to-a-buyer-mid-checkout, written at cart creation and cleared on payment/expiry/abandonment (19.02.04), explicitly distinguished from `held` (owner + day-scale deadline vs no owner + minute-scale countdown), consumed by the manifest invariant (19.01.02 D-06), the per-buyer purchase limit (ticketing-box-office-cx.md#CX-08) and the Operator's read of an unexplained `remaining` dip. (c) Counter table:37 **Remaining** now reads `= capacity − killed − held − comp − paid − carted`, citing D-06's identity verbatim and stating that a unit leaves `remaining` at cart creation and returns on cart expiry (19.02.04 D-04), not at card clearance. (d) Provenance paragraph:39 now names cart create/expire (19.02.04) as `carted`'s writer. (e) Happy Path 1 zeroes `carted` at manifest lock; Happy Path 2 rewritten as the two atomic moves a sale actually is (cart creation: carted+ / remaining−; payment: carted− / paid+, remaining untouched), with the abandoned-cart reversal and the no-cart walk-up path stated. (f) New Edge Case row:59 covers `remaining = 0` caused entirely by carts — Fan sees sold-out and the waitlist (19.02.04 #CX-04), Operator sees the zero with carted stated beside it, mitigation is TTL tuning per on-sale (19.02.04 Q-04), never display. (g) Cross-Cut Notes: the 19.01.02 note now cites D-06's identity as the binding constraint on the whole counter table; a new 19.02.04 note names cart create/expire as `carted`'s sole writer and flags that D-04's source-pool return means `remaining` is not always what rises when `carted` falls. (h) New Open Question Q-04 (Owner: Agent, Deferred To: `/write-architecture-spec` (domain 19.01 ↔ 19.02 ↔ 19.05)). 19.01.02 — (i) Edge Case:122's "User Sees" no longer claims the Operator sees an available figure lower than `remaining`; it now states that `remaining` IS the available-to-hold figure because D-06 already nets carted out, with the carted quantity shown beside it; the "What Happens" cell is strengthened to structurally-impossible rather than merely-refused. (j) States:154 Live row rewritten the same way — was "Available-to-hold shown separately from `remaining` because `carted` is untouchable".

residualQuestion.text: Because `remaining` is net of `carted` (19.01.02 D-06), it can reach zero on carts alone. When those carts then expire at a genuine sell-out, does the returning inventory route through the waitlist or reappear openly on the storefront? 19.01.02 D-09 routes inventory entering public availability at or after sell-out through the waitlist but enumerates only hold release, kill reversal and capacity increase; 19.02.04's own edge case reads "Other fans see inventory reappear", which is open sale. Neither names cart expiry.
residualQuestion.whyItIsNew: Under the pre-fix 19.05.01 formula, carted sat inside remaining, so remaining could never reach zero on carts alone and the boundary case did not exist in the count's model. Correcting the formula to D-06 makes it reachable, and it lands squarely on the domain's anti-bot posture (19.02.04 D-01, 19.01.02 DT-07), so it is tracked rather than silently decided.
